title: Seventh Word Proof For Patience And Reliance Weakness As A Document

questions.question: What are the two medicines named in the passage?
questions.answer: They are trusting Allah with patience, and relying on the Creator’s power while having confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage explain why a person who trusts Allah should not be overwhelmed by fear?
questions.answer: It says such a person depends on the Lord of all things, whose power is unlimited, so even huge troubles do not have to crush him.

questions.question: What words does the person say when facing a severe hardship?
questions.answer: He reminds himself that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of feeling can a person who knows Allah find in weakness?
questions.answer: He can find a kind of peace and sweetness in admitting his weakness before Allah.

questions.question: What example is used to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: The passage gives the example of a baby who feels safest when it knows it is helpless and runs to its mother for protection.

questions.question: What does the example of the baby and mother teach about human weakness?
questions.answer: It teaches that feeling needy is not always bad, because it can lead a person to seek mercy and safety from the one who truly cares for him.

questions.question: How is a mother’s mercy described when compared with Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: A mother’s mercy is described as only a tiny reflection of divine mercy.

questions.question: Why did the wise people gladly admit that they had no real power of their own?
questions.answer: Because they wanted to turn fully to Allah instead of trusting themselves.

questions.question: What did those wise people use as a means of drawing near to Allah?
questions.answer: They used their weakness and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: What main lesson does this passage give about fear and weakness?
questions.answer: It teaches that when fear and weakness push a person toward Allah, they become a source of spiritual strength and comfort.

questions.question: Which qualities are joined together as the first medicine in this passage?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah is joined with patience.

questions.question: Which qualities are joined together as the second medicine in this same section?
questions.answer: Depending on the Creator’s power is joined with confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention Allah’s command that something happens as soon as He wills it?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s power is complete and immediate, so trusting Him is completely reasonable.

questions.question: How should a believer respond to a major disaster according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should turn to Allah, remember that he belongs to Allah, and place his trust in Him.

questions.question: In this passage, is weakness shown as something to hide or as something to recognize before Allah?
questions.answer: It is shown as something to recognize before Allah.

questions.question: What surprising idea does the passage teach about fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that fear of Allah can contain a deep spiritual pleasure.

questions.question: Why is the baby example important to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It makes the lesson easier to understand by showing that helplessness can lead to safety and closeness instead of only pain.

questions.question: What can we infer about self-reliance from this passage?
questions.answer: We can infer that relying only on ourselves is not enough, because human strength is limited.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the wisdom of people who know Allah well?
questions.answer: It describes them as people who willingly admit their weakness and seek refuge in Allah.

questions.question: What is the overall message of this section about the heart of a believer?
questions.answer: A believer’s heart finds security by trusting Allah, accepting human weakness, and depending on His mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What two cures are presented for the human condition in this passage?
questions.answer: One is trust in Allah with patience, and the other is relying on Allah’s power with confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah’s absolute power change the way a person faces hardship?
questions.answer: It gives him courage, because he knows his Lord can do whatever He wills.

questions.question: What statement does the believer make during intense suffering?
questions.answer: He declares that he belongs to Allah and that his return is to Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of person takes comfort in admitting his helplessness?
questions.answer: A person who knows Allah.

questions.question: What emotional lesson is taught through the image of a child running to its mother?
questions.answer: The lesson is that fear can drive a person toward loving protection.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare divine mercy with a mother’s mercy?
questions.answer: It uses something familiar and loving to help the reader understand, while also showing that Allah’s mercy is far greater.

questions.question: What attitude toward personal strength did the wise people reject?
questions.answer: They rejected acting as if they were strong and independent on their own.

questions.question: What did the wise people seek by admitting powerlessness?
questions.answer: They sought Allah’s protection and nearness.

questions.question: If someone says weakness is always bad, how would this passage respond?
questions.answer: It would say weakness becomes good when it leads a person to trust Allah and seek refuge in Him.

questions.question: In this passage, what are believers told to rely on instead of their own limited strength?
questions.answer: They are told to rely on Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: What role does patience play in the first medicine?
questions.answer: Patience helps a person stay steady while trusting Allah during hardship.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a trusting person has less reason to fear?
questions.answer: Because he is under the care of the One whose power reaches everything.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the proper response to calamity?
questions.answer: The proper response is to return to Allah inwardly through trust, remembrance, and surrender.

questions.question: How is fear of Allah different from ordinary fear in this passage?
questions.answer: It is not shown as panic or despair, but as a feeling that brings a person toward mercy and safety.

questions.question: What does the baby illustration suggest about true safety?
questions.answer: True safety comes from being sheltered by one who is loving and stronger than you.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the source of all tender mercy in creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that such mercy comes from Allah and reflects His greater mercy.

questions.question: How did the wise turn weakness into something beneficial?
questions.answer: They used it as a reason to seek Allah instead of trusting themselves.

questions.question: What is one central theme running through the whole passage?
questions.answer: Human weakness becomes a blessing when it leads to dependence on Allah.

questions.question: What are the two pairs of qualities called medicines in the passage?
questions.answer: They are trust with patience, and dependence on Allah’s power with confidence in His wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the fear of someone who depends on Allah?
questions.answer: It says such fear loses its crushing force because the person leans on the all-powerful Lord.

questions.question: What belief helps the person stay calm during the hardest trials?
questions.answer: The belief that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can come from knowing one’s own weakness before Allah?
questions.answer: Comfort, sweetness, and a stronger connection to Allah can come from it.

questions.question: What everyday human relationship is used to explain this spiritual truth?
questions.answer: The relationship between a baby and its mother is used.

questions.question: What is the point of saying that a mother’s mercy is only a small reflection?
questions.answer: The point is to show that Allah’s mercy is much greater than even the gentlest human care.

questions.question: How did the wise people view claims of personal power?
questions.answer: They turned away from such claims and admitted their need for Allah.

questions.question: What did they choose to present before Allah instead of strength?
questions.answer: They presented their weakness and their fear of Him.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of this passage?
questions.answer: Real peace comes from knowing we are weak servants and placing our trust in Allah’s mercy, power, and wisdom.

questions.question: What is meant by the two medicines in this passage?
questions.answer: They are spiritual cures that help a person face life’s hardships through trust in Allah and dependence on Him.

questions.question: What two things does the first medicine combine?
questions.answer: It combines trust in Allah and patience.

questions.question: What two things does the second medicine combine?
questions.answer: It combines relying on the Creator’s power and trusting His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage support the idea that Allah is fully able to help?
questions.answer: It points to His absolute command and power over all things.

questions.question: What should a believer remember when disaster strikes?
questions.answer: He should remember that he belongs to Allah and that his final return is to Allah.

questions.question: What unusual claim does the passage make about fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It says that fear of Allah can bring a kind of joy and comfort.

questions.question: How does the example of the intelligent baby support that claim?
questions.answer: It shows that feeling helpless can be sweet when it leads to protection and closeness.

questions.question: What comparison is made between human mercy and divine mercy?
questions.answer: Human mercy, even a mother’s, is only a tiny sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: What choice did the wise make about their own strength?
questions.answer: They stopped depending on their own strength and sought refuge in Allah.

questions.question: What final lesson does the passage teach about weakness, fear, and faith?
questions.answer: It teaches that weakness and fear are not defeats if they lead a person to trust Allah and seek His care.
